html:
November 4, 2026

Democrats flip both chambers of Congress in midterm sweep

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews

Decision Desk HQ and other outlets projected that Democrats won control of the House of Representatives and the United States Senate in the November 3 midterm elections, the first time the party has held both chambers since 2023. Senate projections put Democrats at 51 or more seats, with early tallies suggesting a House majority that could reach 250 seats. Exit polling cited by newspapers pointed to high prices, the war in Iran and concerns about government corruption as the drivers, with double-digit swings toward Democrats among Latino voters, Catholic voters and voters under 30. Front pages in the United States and abroad described the result as a historic rebuke of President Trump.

Democrats win Texas Senate and governor's races for first time in three decades

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews, @hunteralexanderhowell

State Rep. James Talarico defeated Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton for the U.S. Senate seat in Texas, the first statewide win for a Texas Democrat since 1994. CBS News projected that Democratic state Rep. Gina Hinojosa unseated Gov. Greg Abbott, who was seeking a fourth term and conceded; Hinojosa becomes the state's first Latina governor. Hinojosa campaigned on affordability and public schools, opposed Abbott's school voucher program, and backed a moratorium on new data centers until lawmakers put protections for residents in place, going further than Abbott's pause on new state permits.

Democrats flip Senate seats across deep-red states

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews, @hunteralexanderhowell

Democrats picked up Senate seats in North Carolina, where Roy Cooper defeated Michael Whatley; South Carolina, where Annie Andrews beat appointed Sen. Darline Graham; Kansas, where Adam Hamilton defeated Sen. Roger Marshall; Iowa, where the Democratic candidate defeated Rep. Ashley Hinson; and Maine, where Sen. Susan Collins conceded to Troy Jackson. Kansas had not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1932, and Trump carried South Carolina by nearly 18 points in 2024. Democrats also flipped House seats in unexpected places, including Indiana's 5th District, where J.D. Ford unseated Rep. Victoria Spartz in a district Trump won by 17 points.

Democrats take governorships in Georgia, Ohio, Iowa and beyond

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews, @hunteralexanderhowell

Keisha Lance Bottoms won the Georgia governor's race, defeating Republican Rick Jackson and becoming the first Black woman elected governor in United States history. Amy Acton defeated Vivek Ramaswamy in Ohio, Rob Sand defeated Zach Lahn in Iowa, and David Crowley held Wisconsin for Democrats. Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro won re-election by a wide margin in one of the country's closest swing states.

Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate race to become first Muslim senator

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews, @total.hypocrisy

Decision Desk HQ projected that Democrat Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan's Senate race, holding the seat for Democrats in a state Trump carried by 1.4 points in 2024. El-Sayed, an epidemiologist and former Detroit health director, will be the first Muslim elected to the United States Senate.

Midterms produce more than a dozen electoral firsts

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews

Tuesday's results sent a slate of first-time officeholders to governor's offices, the Senate and state legislatures. Deb Haaland became the first Native American woman elected governor, in New Mexico, and Peggy Flanagan the first Native American woman elected to the Senate, in Minnesota; Chris Pappas won New Hampshire's open Senate seat as the first openly gay man elected to that chamber. Republican Byron Donalds became Florida's first Black governor and Republican Marsha Blackburn the first woman elected to lead Tennessee, while Alabama and Georgia each elected their first openly transgender state legislators.

Vance blames Iran war for Republican midterm losses

tags: politics, war
sources: @groundnews, @aaronparnas

Vice President JD Vance said in a series of posts on X that the war with Iran was the reason his party lost the midterms, writing that "the reason we lost is the war" and that President Trump had said as much the night before. Vance said Republican turnout held up but that many 2024 Trump voters backed Democrats, citing a pollster who found the top reasons were ending the war, the cost of living, an America First focus and changing the relationship with Israel. He challenged Republicans who supported the war to defend it openly and rejected calls for an immigration amnesty, while saying he was open to shifting enforcement toward employers of unauthorized labor.

Trump weighs firing Hegseth as defense secretary faces impeachment vote

tags: politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas

CBS News reported that President Trump is actively considering firing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth following the election results. Hegseth faces a House impeachment vote as soon as next week that is expected to pass. Republican Sen. Thom Tillis said there would be a public reckoning and accountability for Hegseth after the party's losses.

House Democrats promise investigations and public Epstein hearings

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Rep. Robert Garcia, the incoming chair of the House Oversight Committee, issued a two-word statement to Republicans after the results: "lawyer up." Democrats signalled they will pursue the Trump family, administration officials, associates of Jeffrey Epstein and Corey Lewandowski, and Rep. James Walkinshaw said public Epstein hearings will be held. Republicans in Washington were described as expecting subpoenas of the president's children and probes of his companies, with some privately saying they are now willing to break with the White House.

Dow jumps 1,500 points and oil falls 8% after Democratic sweep

tags: markets, economy
sources: @groundnews, @oafnation_actual

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1,514 points, or 2.9%, on Wednesday, climbing above 53,000 for the first time since September 8, while the S&P 500 gained 1.7% and the Nasdaq 1.9%. U.S. crude oil prices fell more than 8% as traders bet the election results would push the administration toward negotiations with Iran; the president said there were no immediate plans to strike the country. Oil had risen more than 10% in October on expectations of post-election escalation. Trump posted that the stock market had hit another record high.

Gulf governments expect Trump to seek Iran deal after losses

tags: politics, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

Two sources familiar with Gulf government thinking told Reuters that another full-scale assault on Iran is less likely after the midterm results and that Trump now has more reason to pursue a peace deal. Oil fell for a third consecutive day on Wednesday as markets priced in renewed talks.

Trump says he will accept results, avoids mentioning them in public remarks

tags: politics
sources: @groundnews, @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Trump posted on Truth Social that he was not on the ballot and would have won in a landslide if he had been, and told The New York Times he would accept the results and expected to work with Democrats. He made no public appearances for much of the day and, in his first on-camera remarks, spoke for more than fifteen minutes about the new White House ballroom, the arch and a golf course without mentioning the election. He also attacked Fox News and called Greg Abbott a RINO in a string of posts. The White House account posted a message reading "PSA: Trump is still your president."

Record $11.9 billion midterm spending draws scrutiny of billionaire donors

tags: politics, elections
sources: @carolinegleich, @groundnews, @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Campaign spending for the 2026 congressional elections is projected to reach $11.9 billion, a record, according to OpenSecrets, with Democratic contenders expected to spend $2.2 billion against $1.4 billion for Republicans. Elon Musk spent close to half a billion dollars, including roughly $200 million in Texas, and lost the races he backed; 172 billionaire families spent a combined $1.7 billion, and roughly one dollar in eight came from undisclosed donors. Musk has reportedly been mass-deleting posts from his X account since the results became public. Critics traced the spending to the 2010 Citizens United decision and cited polling showing 72% of Americans believe there is too much money in politics.

Whistleblowers describe ICE stand-down order for Election Day

tags: immigration, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

DHS whistleblowers said that beginning November 1, orders for a "national no enforcement day" spread to ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations officers through internal leadership channels and word of mouth, directing a halt to all enforcement operations on Election Day. ICE tracking sites and community alert networks reported some of the lowest levels of activity this year on November 3, with most sightings being parked vehicles. It is unclear where the order originated or whether every ICE region received it.

Newsom threatens ICE prosecutions as DOJ sends target letters to Democrats

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

California Gov. Gavin Newsom threatened to jail ICE officials who illegally appear at polling places to intimidate voters in the state. The New York Times confirmed that the Justice Department sent roughly 20 target letters to Democrats, including the election lawyer Marc Elias, indicating they may be targets of a possible criminal prosecution.

Voters split on election rules, abortion and taxes in statewide ballot measures

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews, @carolinegleich

Around 145 statewide measures appeared on ballots, with voters approving abortion-rights amendments in Nevada and Virginia and rejecting a Missouri measure that would have restored a near-total ban, while Idaho's legalization measure failed. Voter ID measures passed in Ohio and North Carolina but failed in California and Colorado, and several states wrote citizens-only voting rules into their constitutions. Florida approved a major property tax cut that a state estimate says could cost local governments up to $12 billion a year; Utah voters rejected Amendment B, which would have required 60% approval for citizen tax initiatives, by 62% to 38%.

Senate results seen blocking Republican Supreme Court appointments for years

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Republicans believe the Democratic Senate majority makes it highly improbable that they can confirm a Supreme Court justice for close to a decade, given the Senate map in 2028 and 2030. That assessment complicates retirement plans for Justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas, with Alito seen as likely to step down within the next year.

Mike Johnson exits Republican leadership as succession fight begins

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Speaker Mike Johnson said he will not run for House minority leader and is leaving Republican leadership. Jim Jordan and Steve Scalise are both running to lead the House Republican conference.

Mississippi Senate race separated by 43 votes with no runoff

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews

Democrat Scott Colom led Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by 43 votes in Mississippi's Senate race as of 3 a.m. Wednesday, with 95.6% of votes counted: 462,821 to 462,778, with independent Ty Pinkins taking 19,935. Because it is a general election for a congressional seat, Mississippi will hold no runoff and the candidate with the most votes wins. Neither candidate declared victory, though both said they expected to hold the seat.

Republicans hold Florida Senate seat as Democrats overperform in House races

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews, @aaronparnas

Decision Desk HQ projected that Ashley Moody held Florida's U.S. Senate seat for Republicans, defeating Democrat Angie Nixon in a state Trump carried by 13.1 points in 2024. Democrats nonetheless ran strongly in House races across the state, including Rep. Kathy Castor's win in Florida's 14th District after Republicans redrew the map, and close contests against Anna Paulina Luna and Maria Elvira Salazar.

Ossoff holds Georgia Senate seat

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews

Decision Desk HQ projected that Sen. Jon Ossoff won re-election in Georgia, holding the seat for Democrats in a state Trump carried by 2.2 points in 2024. Republicans had targeted the seat from the start of Trump's second term.

Israel certifies election leaving Netanyahu's bloc short of a majority

tags: politics, elections
sources: @oafnation_actual

Israel's Central Elections Committee certified the October 27 results on Wednesday and found no evidence of the fraud Netanyahu had alleged, according to the Associated Press. Netanyahu's bloc took 53 seats, eight short of a majority. President Herzog accepted the count and is beginning coalition talks.

Trump says US aid to Israel ends at year's end

tags: politics, defence
sources: @ericmoutsos

In an interview before the midterms, Trump said American aid to Israel, roughly four billion dollars a year, will be cut off at the end of the year, saying Israel no longer needs it, while adding that help would be available if it were needed. He also said he has a 99% approval rating in Israel and joked he could move there and become prime minister. In the same stretch of remarks, Speaker Mike Johnson warned Republicans that losing the midterms would turn every congressional committee into an investigative body targeting the president's family, cabinet and donors.

Europe's far-right leaders distance themselves from Trump over Iran war

tags: politics, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

France's Jordan Bardella said U.S. intervention in Iran carries heavy economic consequences, according to Reuters, and Germany's Alice Weidel said a broken non-intervention promise had haunted Republicans. Analysts told Reuters that ties to Trump now risk becoming a liability for European far-right parties.

Air Force seeks new cruise missile for Ukraine

tags: defence, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Air Force has asked industry for a new Ukraine cruise missile under the ERAM program, seeking a 500-pound weapon with a range over 250 nautical miles, according to Defense News. First deliveries of 1,000 or more would begin three months after award, with a request-for-information deadline of November 19.

Pentagon offers drone maker up to $450 million to close gap with China

tags: defence, tech
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Office of Strategic Capital announced a conditional loan of up to $450 million to Neros Technologies, according to the company. Combined with $165 million in private funds, the $615 million project targets production of one million U.S. drones a year by 2028.

Latvia says Russian and Ukrainian drones violated its airspace

tags: defence, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

Latvia's military said a drone that crossed its border on Sunday was a Russian Geran type that flew back over the frontier, while a drone on Monday was likely Ukrainian and crashed inside Latvia, according to Reuters. NATO jets were activated on Monday as the war in Ukraine continues to spill into allied airspace.

FDA grants tentative approval to low-cost generic HIV prevention shot

tags: health
sources: @groundnews

The FDA gave tentative approval to Dr. Reddy's low-cost generic version of lenacapavir, a twice-yearly injection for HIV prevention. The drug could cost about $40 a year in low- and middle-income countries, compared with more than $28,000 for Gilead's U.S. brand, and may speed access in 120 countries.
